summary: Scott County, AR steel fire tower in the Ouachita NF; sources conflict on a 1934 vs 1942 build and on 33 vs 50 ft; listed surplus by 1970 and since removed.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a cabin at the top
facts.status_note: Listed as surplus by 1970 and described as removed, with no removal date given
facts.agency: Ouachita National Forest (Oden and Cold Springs ranger districts)

events.note: Directory heading says constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps
Steel tower of 33 feet with a 7 by 7 foot cab, per the fire tower book quoted in the directory; that passage calls it most likely the second tower on the site
Oden Ranger District no longer used the tower
Cold Springs Ranger District manned it during periods of high danger and low visibility (letter dated January 6, 1959)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The fire tower book quoted in the directory gives 33 feet; the 1956 Geodetic Survey description gives about 50 feet. The record keeps 15.2 m (about 50 ft) from the survey, and the story reports both figures.

sources.title: Lookouts of the Mena & Oden Ranger Districts, Arkansas

notes_for_editor: The 1934 CCC date and the 1942 steel tower date both appear in the directory page, and the story reports both; the 1934 date may refer to an earlier structure, but no source says so, and it is unresolved. The fire tower book and the Geodetic Survey text were read only as quoted on the directory page; no separate URL was found for either. The removal date is not given. Staffing emergency as of 1959 is my reading of manned during periods of high danger. The spelling Abbot appears only on argenweb. argenweb lists it among the towers that once stood and says only Rich Mountain, Bee Mountain and Tall Peak remain standing today. No source describes the summit today or public access.
